pull_request.title: Software: Assemble the PR29 pixel barrels in DD4hep
pull_request.head: implementation/dd4hep-pixel-barrel
pull_request.body:
Implements the human-selected, cable-inclusive PR #29 pixel barrel baseline as a standalone DD4hep prototype: four layers, 82 staves, 2,750 modules and 6,206 sensitive chip patches, with outward supports, CO₂ tubes, mounting rings/feet and cumulative barrel service material. This PR is stacked on the unmerged `design/pixel-barrel-support` branch.

Reusable C++ module/stave/mount/service builders keep the assembly factory concise. Repository CMake, a pinned-input compact exporter and physical validation make shape/material updates repeatable. DES-012 governs this implementation; related module provenance is issue #7 / DES-001. The human baseline selection is recorded without advancing formal design sign-off.

The requested provisional cable recipe is configurable in `detector/config/pixel-barrel.json`: **10% Cu / 40% polyimide / 50% air by cable-footprint volume**, before separate routing packing void. DD4hep receives converted mass fractions. Retained 5%/10%/20% Cu runs preserve geometry, identifiers, ray paths and all non-cable materials; modeled barrel masses are 20.345/24.054/31.472 kg. The default is a hypothesis for expert review, not a measured cable specification.

Validation actually run on installed DD4hep 1.38 / ROOT 6.40.04:

- CMake build and CTest **3/3 pass**: ten pure Python controls, full DD4hep physical validation, and ROOT colour export/reopen verification.
- All 39,386 expected entities audited; all 6,206 sensitive centres/normals match the pinned layout.
- **Zero overlaps/extrusions at 10⁻⁵ mm** in all three material variants.
- 6,206 unique volume IDs and 31,030 pixel cell-address/centre roundtrips, including chip edges.
- 75 deterministic ROOT navigation/material rays per variant; all four pixel layers exercised.
- Dashboard records/build, fixture/link/history checks, session logging and whitespace checks pass. Pure exporter checks added to CI; DD4hep runtime checks require the documented local environment.

Implementation refinements requiring review: 0.255 mm graphite ASIC contact shims fill the existing module-to-support gap; non-overlapping effective end-bay cells preserve the original cable/Ti/CO₂ inventories while smearing illustrative turns. Module bonds/bump metals/connectors/manifolds/fasteners remain incomplete inventory. Geant4 transport, ACTS conversion, thermal/hydraulic/mechanical qualification and full-detector integration are future gates. No previous study evidence or sensor placement was changed.

Entry points: `detector/README.md`, `docs/design/DES-012-dd4hep-pixel-barrels.md`, `docs/validation/DES-012/results.md` and paired session record `SESSION-2026-09-30-dd4hep-pixel-barrel`. Source, configuration, library and report hashes are retained. Node preflight detected changed setup/lockfile fingerprints; actual task capabilities were reverified without changing shared dependencies.



Material display colours are now assigned consistently by material family through `detector/config/display.json`. Standard ROOT indices and transparency are stored on volumes, including nested tubes/coolant. A fresh ROOT-only process reopened the export and verified all **36,550 placed solid volume styles** without recolouring. Counts, masses, material properties, navigation rays, identifiers and overlap results remain exactly equal to the retained nominal physics results. `export_root.py` provides a repeatable export plus persistence check; the README includes geoDisplay and ROOT viewing commands. Evidence: `docs/validation/DES-012/display/results.md`.

issues.title: Design reusable RD53 pixel-module alternatives
issues.body:
Develop DES-001 as a stand-alone RD53 pixel-module proposal with reusable structures, few module types, low material and realistic manufacture, services and thermal interfaces. The available RD53 chip is fixed; the exact inventory variant is being clarified. Pixel volume/layer layout is not selected by this task.

The Tracking Engineer leads two independent alternatives, each with top-view and cross-section drawings, source facts/derivations/design choices and explicit limitations. The Project Coordinator supplies a balanced comparison and conditional recommendation after technical synthesis.

Public RD53 documentation and ATLAS/CMS detector/upgrade TDRs are references, not an instruction to copy either experiment. Catalogue every new normative source in reference/manifest.yaml, distinguish RD53A from production successors, and leave unverified thickness/power/irradiation assumptions visible. Include active/inactive area, chip tiling, bumps, flex/adhesive/bonds, sensor bias/isolation, material accounting and credible cooling/power/data handoffs. Layout fit, radiation requirements, engineering tolerances and production sign-off remain separate gates.

Scope: DRAFT designs and source/design study evidence only; no detector geometry or reconstruction changes. Update project tracking in the same PR. Existing context: stage B/C of PLAN-NODD-001, global envelope baseline DES-003 / ADR-006, with the formal-sign-off documentation discrepancy preserved.

events.text:
DES-012 records the implementation contract before code integration. The human
selected a working baseline and authorized provisional materials; no formal
SIGNED OFF/ACCEPTED lifecycle transition was recorded. The compact is isolated
from full-detector production geometry.

Provisional cable composition is configurable by volume: 10% Cu, 40% polyimide,
50% air before separate routing packing void. Volume inventories are converted
to DD4hep mass fractions. Sensitivity variants use 5%/20% Cu, preserving geometry.
Local cooling is nested foam/Ti/CO₂; mounting preserves the inherited rings/feet.
End-bay effective cells partition the earlier illustrative service turns and
preserve constituent inventory. Explicit graphite shims fill the sensor/ASIC-to-
support gap within the inherited module envelope. Omitted hardware, liquid-density
upper bound and effective compositions remain visible in DES-012.

events.text:
Recommend nodehammer for optional visual review. Heavy importers are not in its
standard wheel, so a pinned source build enables TGeo/DD4hep and native viewing.
No shared Spack installation was changed. The build helper uses an isolated
Conan environment with the active Spack Python, local profile/cache, retained
recipe lock and binary provenance. Source pin is
30b19dcbd9329b742d98b1383a1484600fc3e0c3; no upstream patch was applied.

The preparation helper checks every named detector entity against expected.json,
then repeats the check through the portable NHB representation. It exports
full, sensitive-only and single-stave projects plus GLBs with verified metre
units and material alpha/BLEND. The full scene keeps physical parents with
children and excludes only world/assembly boxes. Generated styles follow the
existing nODD palette. Source compact and geometry remain unchanged.

All 39386 detector entities match; maximum centre error is 1.14e-13 mm.
All 6206 sensitive tags/normals survive. The full view has 36550 physical mesh
placements, including 492 boolean feet. Native complete/cutaway PNGs were
rendered and inspected. ROOT fallback also imports 39388 nodes but lacks tags.
The report records provenance, inputs, commands and hashes; absolute command
prefixes were normalized to documented checkout placeholders for retention.

Limitations are explicit: native BLEND pending, no parent/daughter material
subtraction, potential coplanar silicon-face artifacts, internal IDs reindexed,
no packed-cell-ID reconstruction claim, browser runtime not qualified. Strict
conversion incorrectly rejects informational diagnostics and ROOT suffix
recognition is defective at the pinned revision. The workflow uses structured
import diagnostics plus placement audits and an explicit TGeo format flag.
